policy.title: Benchmark evidence policy
policy.summary: Benchmarks are supporting evidence, not our final ranking. We identify the exact model/version, source, snapshot date and harness. Product scores are not treated as model scores, and results from different harness versions are not compared directly.

sources.name: Arena Text Leaderboard
sources.measures: Human preference in anonymous model-vs-model battles across open-ended text tasks.
sources.caveat: A product such as ChatGPT or Claude can change its default model; Arena ranks specific model versions, not the whole product.

sources.name: Arena-Rank methodology
sources.measures: Bradley-Terry ratings with reweighting and confidence intervals from pairwise preference data.
sources.use_for: Explaining how Arena scores are produced
sources.caveat: Human preference can reward style and verbosity; it is not an objective factuality test.

sources.name: SWE-bench Verified
sources.measures: Percentage of 500 human-validated real GitHub issues resolved by a coding model or agent.
sources.caveat: Scores depend heavily on the agent harness. mini-SWE-agent v1.x and v2.x results are not directly comparable.

sources.name: LiveBench
sources.measures: Objective, frequently refreshed tasks across reasoning, math, coding, language, instruction following and data analysis.
sources.caveat: Always state the release; questions and model configurations change between snapshots. Checked 2026-09-14: the repository is live, but its public changelog stops at 2026-01-08 and its README still shows "Top models as of 30th September 2024". livebench.ai renders client-side only, so no dated leaderboard could be read without a browser. Treat LiveBench as release-pinned evidence, not a current ranking.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis methodology
sources.measures: Independent intelligence, latency, speed, price, speech, image and video model evaluations.
sources.use_for: Cost/speed context and non-text modality methodology
sources.caveat: API model measurements do not equal the complete end-user product experience.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard (frozen; subdomain now serves 4.0)
sources.measures: Accuracy of an agent + model + reasoning-effort configuration on 89 complex containerized terminal tasks.
sources.use_for: Coding agents and terminal-capable development tools
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14: https://www.tbench.ai/leaderboard/terminal-bench/2.1 returns a 308 redirect to https://www.tbench.ai/?version=2.1, and every route on that host — including ?version=2.1 — served the Terminal-Bench 4.0 board (title "TERMINAL-BENCH 4.0", leaderboard slug "4-0-0"). No 2.1 rows could be read from this URL on that date, and no archived 2.1 board was found on the site. Never present this as a model-only score; keep agent, exact model, effort, trial count and integrity metadata visible.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Image methodology
sources.measures: Blind pairwise image preference with exact model/version and matched prompt conditions.
sources.caveat: Keep text-to-image and editing pools separate; old model versions are historical evidence only.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Video methodology
sources.measures: Modality-separated video quality, latency and price comparisons.
sources.caveat: Do not compare Elo across different video modalities or output settings.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis TTS methodology
sources.measures: Provider-voice and controlled-voice human-preference comparisons for text-to-speech.
sources.caveat: Controlled-voice and provider-voice arenas answer different questions and must remain separate.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench: Cursor CLI + Grok 4.5 submission
sources.measures: Maintainer-verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 submission record for one exact Cursor CLI configuration.
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14 against the raw submission file: Cursor CLI 2026.07.08-0c04a8a + cursor/grok-4.5 at high effort, 79.33% +/- 1.46, 445 trials, 8.99% reward-hack disqualifications, dated 2026-07-09. The record is unchanged. Two limits sit on it: the Terminal-Bench 2.1 README states "Community submissions are currently closed for Terminal-Bench 2.1", so the 2.1 board is frozen, and the live 4.0 board carries no Cursor entry, so there is no current Cursor reading to compare it to. Scores from 2.1 and 4.0 are different harness versions and must never be compared with each other.

sources.name: Harbor Hub — Terminal-Bench 2.1 dataset
sources.measures: The live dataset record for Terminal-Bench 2.1: which tasks the frozen board ran and which version is published.
sources.use_for: Confirming the task set behind a Terminal-Bench 2.1 configuration score
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14: the dataset page reports "Displaying 89 of 89 tasks" and "Version 2.1 of Terminal-Bench", so 89 tasks is the verified count for 2.1 — the 4.0 board is a different, larger task set. This page publishes the task list, not leaderboard scores; it cannot upgrade a 2.1 score into a 4.0 score.

snapshot_summary: All six tracked Arena listings were re-read from the 13 Sep 2026 snapshot (vote cutoff 2026-09-13, 8,146,274 votes across 402 models). Every row holds the same exact model version as before. Three ratings moved by one point (DeepSeek, Gemini, Mistral) and three were unchanged; all six ranks moved down by 2-3 places and all six vote counts were revised downward as Arena re-filtered battles. Ratings moved by at most one point against confidence intervals of +/-2 to +/-7, so this is leaderboard drift, not evidence that any product got worse.
